origin.description: Format text and print it in columns.
origin.usage: utf8_print(x, chars = NULL, quote = TRUE, print.gap = NULL, right = FALSE, max = NULL, names = NULL, rownames = NULL, escapes = NULL, display = TRUE, style = TRUE, utf8 = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Text, a list, or a dict of names to text.

arguments.name: chars
arguments.text: Display units kept from each element.

arguments.name: line_width
arguments.text: Columns wrap at this width. R reads getOption("width").

origin.details: Names sit above the values. The return value is x, invisibly.
origin.value: The same object, after printing it.

translation.description: A dict is a named vector. A list is printed with index labels.
translation.usage: utf8_print(x, chars=None, quote=True, right=False, max_print=None, line_width=80, file=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Text, a list, or a dict of names to text.

arguments.name: chars
arguments.text: Display units kept from each element.

arguments.name: line_width
arguments.text: Columns wrap at this width. R reads getOption("width").

translation.details: The printed row keeps the field padding. The function returns x.
translation.value: The same object, after printing it.
translation.example:
from utf8 import utf8_print
utf8_print({"a": "fa\u00e7ile", "b": "x"}, chars=3)
